newsitem.title: UK: Police investigate reports of Belfast explosion.
newsitem.headline: Police investigate reports of Belfast explosion.

text.p: Northern Irish police said on Sunday they had received reports of an explosion in a Catholic district of north Belfast.
A spokesman could not confirm whether it had been caused by a bomb. "We have received first reports of an explosion somewhere in Ardoyne. That's all we know," the spokesman told Reuters.
The explosion was reported against a background of mounting tension in Northern Ireland.

The Irish Republican Army, fighting to oust Britain from Northern Ireland, claimed responsibility on Friday for shooting a policeman who was guarding a prominent Protestant politician visiting his young son in hospital.
The shooting was the first IRA shooting attack since the guerrillas ended their truce last February and sparked fears their extremist Protestant foes would call off their own two-year old truce.

David Ervine, a leader of the political arm of the outlawed Ulster Volunteer Force, said on Saturday the IRA was intent on provoking an end to the Loyalist militas' ceasefire. "My belief is that it is an attempt to provoke Loyalists to retaliate. My fear is that it is more likely than not that they will succeed," Ervine told Reuters.
